{{nihongo|'''Ikawadani Sōja'''|伊川谷惣社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Harima Province]].

'''Ikawadani Sōsha''' (いかわだにそうしゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Ikawadani-chō Kamiwaki, Nishi Ward, Kobe City, Hyōgo Prefecture. It is considered one of the shrines identified with the Mononobe Shrine listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}. Its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. It is also called '''Sōsha Shrine'''.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, on her return from the {{ill|Three Han Campaign|Q11249435|qid=Q11249435}}, {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} stopped at this place and enshrined {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto}}, which is said to mark the founding of the shrine. This account resembles the descriptions in the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935}} regarding the founding of {{ill|Hirota Shrine (Osaka City)|Q1466105|qid=Q1466105}}, {{ill|Ikuta Shrine|Q710086|qid=Q710086}}, {{ill|Nagata Shrine|Q661395|qid=Q661395}}, and {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|Q705949|qid=Q705949}}, but there is no mention of this shrine in the Nihon Shoki.

It is said that after a period of decline, the shrine was rebuilt in the 3rd year of {{ill|Enkyū|Q1193638|qid=Q1193638}} ({{ill|1071|Q19432|qid=Q19432}}).

Perhaps because it was deeply revered by the local community, the area around the shrine has come to be called “Kijinyama” (Demon God Mountain).

=== Annual Festival ===
Every year, the autumn festival is held on the first Saturday and Sunday of October.
During the autumn festival, {{ill|Futon Daiko|Q11277203|qid=Q11277203}} and {{ill|Lion dance|Q713866|qid=Q713866}} are dedicated.
